knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: Mao J, Doshi U, Wright M, Hop CECA, Li AP, Chen Y. Prediction of
  the Pharmacokinetics of Pravastatin as an OATP Substrate Using Plateable
  Human Hepatocytes With Human Plasma Data and PBPK Modeling. CPT
  Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol. 2018;7(4):251-258.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12283>
* PubMed Central open-access copy: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5915609/>

The paper measured the net active (OATP-mediated, rifampicin-sensitive) uptake
of pravastatin into plated human hepatocytes in two incubation media and fitted
each data set with a Michaelis-Menten model. It contributes two model files,
one per medium:

```{r models}
mod_pl <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mao_2018_pravastatin_invitro_plasma"))
mod_him <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mao_2018_pravastatin_invitro_him"))

# Fixed and estimated ini() values are not returned as columns by rxSolve(), so
# read them straight off the packaged model when a check needs one.
ini_val <- function(mod, nm) {
  stopifnot(nm %in% mod$iniDf$name)
  mod$iniDf$est[mod$iniDf$name == nm]
}
```

# Scope: what this paper does and does not contribute

The paper has two layers.

1. **In vitro uptake kinetics (packaged).** Plated cryopreserved hepatocytes
   from one donor were incubated with ten pravastatin concentrations
   (0.14-400 uM) for 0 and 3 minutes, with and without rifampicin. The
   rifampicin-sensitive part of the 3-minute uptake was fitted by
   Michaelis-Menten kinetics: Jmax 134.4 pmol/min/million cells and apparent
   Km 76.77 uM in 100% human plasma (Figure 1), and Jmax 28.49
   pmol/min/million cells and Km 11.72 uM in protein-free hepatocyte induction
   medium (Discussion; Supplementary Figure S1).
2. **Simcyp v15 full-PBPK simulation (not packaged).** Those constants replace
   the OATP1B1 input of the Simcyp default pravastatin compound profile, which
   is then used to simulate the intravenous (9.4 mg) and oral (0.0372-60 mg)
   plasma profiles. Table 1 prints the compound-level inputs only. The tissue
   partition coefficients come from the Rodgers and Rowland prediction method
   (a named method, not values). Absorption uses the ADAM and MechPeff models,
   renal clearance uses Simcyp's mechanistic kidney model, and hepatocellularity,
   liver weight, organ volumes, blood flows and transporter abundances are
   platform defaults that are printed nowhere. No Simcyp workspace was
   deposited. The PBPK layer therefore cannot be reconstructed from the
   publication and is described here only as context.

# In vitro system

```{r population}
str(mod_pl$population)
```

Both assays used hepatocyte lot HH1057 (a 33-year-old Caucasian female donor)
seeded at 350,000 cells/well on collagen-coated 24-well plates. The lot
expressed OATP1B1 at 18.3 and OATP1B3 at 1.7 fmol/million cells. Because the
hepatocyte assay cannot separate the two isoforms, the authors assigned all
active uptake to OATP1B1. In plasma medium the inhibitor was 125 uM
rifampicin (Methods). In induction medium it was 25 uM (Supplementary
Methods).

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Net uptake = (3 min - 0 min, alone) - (3 min - 0 min, + rifampicin) | equation | Methods, 'Absolute intracellular pravastatin concentration' and 'Net pravastatin uptake calculation' |
| Michaelis-Menten fit on nominal concentration | equation | Methods, 'Net pravastatin uptake calculation' (GraphPad Prism 7) |
| `lvmax` (plasma) | log(134.4) pmol/min/million cells | Abstract; Results; Table 1 'Jmax, OATP' |
| `lkm` (plasma) | log(76.77) uM | Abstract; Results; Table 1 'Km, OATP' |
| `fu_inc` (plasma) | 0.485, fixed | Table 1 'fu,inc ... Same as fu,p'; Methods, 'Clearance' |
| `lvmax` (HIM) | log(28.49) pmol/min/million cells | Discussion, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure S2 and S3 captions |
| `lkm` (HIM) | log(11.72) uM | Discussion, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure S2 and S3 captions |
| `fu_inc` (HIM) | 0.98, fixed | Supplementary Figure S2 and S3 captions (the Discussion prints 0.96) |
| `addSd` | 0, fixed | not reported |
| `km_u = km * fu_inc` | derived | Discussion: "the apparent Km was corrected with human plasma protein binding" |
| `clint_uptake = vmax / km` | derived | linear limit of the Michaelis-Menten law |

## Dimensional analysis

`vmax` is in pmol/min/million cells and the medium concentration in uM, so
`uptake = vmax * C / (km + C)` is in pmol/min/million cells and its integral
`hep_pravastatin` is in pmol/million cells. `vmax / km` is in
(pmol/min/million cells)/uM = uL/min/million cells, the unit of the Simcyp
`CLint,T` inputs in Table 1 and Supplementary Table S1.

# Simulation

Each nominal concentration of the assay is placed in the medium at time 0 and
the cells are followed for the 3-minute incubation. These are ten
concentrations per medium, not subjects.

```{r simulate}
conc_nominal <- c(0.14, 0.4, 1.2, 3.7, 11.1, 33.3, 100, 200, 300, 400)

make_events <- function(conc) {
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = seq_along(conc), time = 0, amt = conc, evid = 1,
    cmt = "pravastatin", conc = conc
  )
  obs <- expand.grid(id = seq_along(conc), time = c(0, 1, 2, 3))
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$evid <- 0
  obs$cmt <- "hep_pravastatin"
  obs$conc <- conc[obs$id]
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

# The models carry no inter-individual variability (one donor lot), so
# rxode2's "multi-subject simulation without omega" notice is expected and
# muffled; every other warning still surfaces.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}

sim_medium <- function(mod, label, conc = conc_nominal) {
  ev <- make_events(conc)
  out <- withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, keep = "conc", returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
  out$medium <- label
  out
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_medium(mod_pl, "100% human plasma"),
  sim_medium(mod_him, "Induction medium (HIM)")
)

# The assay's datum: 3-min accumulated net uptake divided by 3 min.
rates <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 3) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rate_assay = hep_pravastatin / 3) |>
  dplyr::select(medium, conc, rate_assay, uptake, km_u, clint_uptake, clint_uptake_u)
knitr::kable(rates, digits = 3)
```

The accumulated state is exactly linear in time, because the fit treated the
medium concentration as constant, so the 3-minute rate equals the
instantaneous rate:

```{r check-linear}
stopifnot(max(abs(rates$rate_assay - rates$uptake) / rates$uptake) < 1e-6)
```

# Replicating Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure S1

The maintainers digitised the plotted means from Figure 1 and Supplementary
Figure S1 at native resolution, calibrating on the axis tick marks. The five
lowest concentrations (0.14-3.7 uM) overlap at the origin and could not be
resolved, so only the six highest are used.

```{r digitised}
digitised <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    medium = "100% human plasma",
    conc = c(11.1, 33.3, 100, 200, 300, 400),
    rate = c(12.39, 34.81, 69.62, 120.35, 103.83, 102.06)
  ),
  data.frame(
    medium = "Induction medium (HIM)",
    conc = c(11.1, 33.3, 100, 200, 300, 400),
    rate = c(13.44, 18.84, 37.31, 21.98, 21.23, 29.27)
  )
)
```

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Net active hepatic uptake rate of pravastatin against nominal concentration. Replicates Figure 1 (100% human plasma) and Supplementary Figure S1 (induction medium) of Mao 2018. Points: digitised published means (N = 3); line: packaged model."}
curve_grid <- expand.grid(
  conc = seq(0, 500, by = 2.5),
  medium = c("100% human plasma", "Induction medium (HIM)"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
mm_par <- data.frame(
  medium = c("100% human plasma", "Induction medium (HIM)"),
  vmax = exp(c(ini_val(mod_pl, "lvmax"), ini_val(mod_him, "lvmax"))),
  km = exp(c(ini_val(mod_pl, "lkm"), ini_val(mod_him, "lkm")))
)
curve_grid <- dplyr::left_join(curve_grid, mm_par, by = "medium") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rate = vmax * conc / (km + conc))

ggplot(curve_grid, aes(conc, rate)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = rates, aes(conc, rate_assay), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = digitised, aes(conc, rate), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~medium, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Pravastatin concentration (uM)",
    y = "Active hepatic uptake rate\n(pmol/min/million cells)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Rate at Km is half of Jmax

```{r check-half}
# Solve each packaged model with the medium set to its own Km and read the
# 3-min rate off the accumulated state.
half <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_medium(mod_pl, "100% human plasma", conc = mm_par$km[1]),
  sim_medium(mod_him, "Induction medium (HIM)", conc = mm_par$km[2])
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 3) |>
  # Drop the solved `vmax`/`km` columns so the join does not suffix them.
  dplyr::select(medium, conc, hep_pravastatin) |>
  dplyr::left_join(mm_par, by = "medium") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rate_at_km = hep_pravastatin / 3,
    ratio = rate_at_km / vmax
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(medium, conc, vmax, rate_at_km, ratio)
knitr::kable(half, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(half$ratio - 0.5) < 1e-6))
```

## Re-fitting the digitised means recovers the printed constants

Fitting the Michaelis-Menten law to the digitised means reproduces the
published Jmax and Km. This checks that each printed pair belongs to the
figure it is attributed to, in particular that the Discussion's 28.49 / 11.72
pair is the induction-medium fit of Supplementary Figure S1. The paper fitted
the individual replicates and the five lowest concentrations as well, so an
exact match is not expected.

```{r check-refit}
refit <- digitised |>
  dplyr::group_by(medium) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(function(d, key) {
    f <- stats::nls(rate ~ jm * conc / (k + conc), data = d, start = list(jm = 100, k = 50))
    data.frame(jmax_refit = unname(coef(f)["jm"]), km_refit = unname(coef(f)["k"]))
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::left_join(mm_par, by = "medium") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    jmax_pct_diff = 100 * (jmax_refit - vmax) / vmax,
    km_pct_diff = 100 * (km_refit - km) / km
  )
refit |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Medium" = medium,
    "Jmax re-fit" = jmax_refit,
    "Km re-fit (uM)" = km_refit,
    "Jmax published" = vmax,
    "Km published (uM)" = km,
    "Jmax diff (%)" = jmax_pct_diff,
    "Km diff (%)" = km_pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(refit$jmax_pct_diff) < 10),
  all(abs(refit$km_pct_diff) < 15)
)
```

Jmax is recovered within a few percent in both media. Km is recovered within
about 10%. Swapping the two pairs between media would miss Jmax by roughly
fivefold.

# Unbound uptake clearance against the published PBPK inputs

The quantity that drives hepatic uptake at clinical concentrations, which are
far below Km, is the unbound linear-range intrinsic clearance
`vmax / (km * fu_inc)`. Supplementary Table S1 compares the OATP1B1 inputs of
earlier pravastatin PBPK models.

```{r check-clint}
clint <- rates |>
  dplyr::distinct(medium, km_u, clint_uptake, clint_uptake_u)
knitr::kable(clint, digits = 3)

# Supplementary Table S1 (uL/min/million cells): the Simcyp default value fitted
# to in vivo data, and the sandwich-culture value of Varma 2012 / Jones 2012
# after its empirical scaling factor of 31.
table_s1 <- data.frame(
  source = c("Simcyp default (fitted in vivo)", "Sandwich-cultured hepatocytes x SF 31"),
  clint_t = c(14.057, 1.9 * 31)
)
knitr::kable(table_s1, digits = 1)

# The two media should give similar unbound clearances: the paper reports that
# both reproduce the in vivo profiles without a scaling factor.
ratio_media <- clint$clint_uptake_u[clint$medium == "100% human plasma"] /
  clint$clint_uptake_u[clint$medium == "Induction medium (HIM)"]
ratio_media
stopifnot(ratio_media > 1, ratio_media < 2)
```

The two media agree within 1.5-fold on the unbound uptake clearance
(`r round(clint$clint_uptake_u[1], 2)` and
`r round(clint$clint_uptake_u[2], 2)` uL/min/million cells). They differ
almost fivefold in Jmax and more than threefold in unbound Km. This is
consistent with the paper's finding that either pair, entered unscaled, lets
the Simcyp model reproduce the intravenous profile. Both values are well below
the 14.057 uL/min/million cells that the Simcyp default fitted to in vivo
data. The PBPK layer is not packaged, so this vignette cannot test whether that
difference is offset by the Km-dependent saturation, the higher hepatocyte
scaling or other Simcyp inputs.

# Published results not reproduced here

* Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure S2: Simcyp simulations of the 9.4 mg
  intravenous profile (mean predicted AUC 0.60 uM.h, against 0.43 uM.h with the
  default profile).
* Figure 3 and Supplementary Figure S3: Simcyp simulations of the 0.0372, 18.23,
  20, 40 and 60 mg oral profiles, and the Cmax and AUC comparison of
  Supplementary Table S2.
* Supplementary Table S3: rifampicin and gemfibrozil AUC ratios simulated with
  the Simcyp inhibitor library files.

All of these are outputs of the platform PBPK layer (see Scope). There is no
plasma concentration-time output to analyse, so no PKNCA non-compartmental
analysis applies to this in vitro model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Medium concentration held constant.** The paper fitted the net uptake rate
  against the nominal concentration, so `d/dt(pravastatin) <- 0`. The
  incubation volume during uptake is not stated, so depletion of the medium
  could not be modelled in any case.
* **Observation is the accumulated net uptake** (`hep_pravastatin`,
  pmol/million cells), not `Cc`. The paper's reported datum is this amount
  divided by the 3-minute window. `checkModelConventions()` warns that the
  observation variable is not canonical. The warning is accepted, because
  renaming the state to `Cc` would misstate what is observed and its units.
* **No residual error.** The paper reports no residual model for the
  GraphPad fit, so `addSd` is fixed to 0. The +/- values printed with Jmax and
  Km (14.3 and 27.4 in plasma; 3.11 and 6.83 in induction medium) are standard
  errors of the regression, not between-donor variability. One donor lot was
  used, so the models carry no inter-individual variability.
* **fu,inc in induction medium: 0.98 vs 0.96.** The Discussion gives 0.96
  (citing Menochet 2012), while both Supplementary Figure S2 and S3 captions,
  which list the simulation inputs, give 0.98. The model carries 0.98. The
  choice changes only the derived `km_u` and `clint_uptake_u`, by 2%.
* **Rifampicin concentration differs by medium.** The main Methods give
  125 uM rifampicin for the plasma-medium assay. The Supplementary Methods,
  which describe the induction-medium incubation, give 25 uM. The model
  describes the net rifampicin-sensitive uptake and has no inhibitor term, so
  this difference is recorded here only.
* **Digitised data.** The points in the figure are means digitised from the
  published figures. The five lowest concentrations were not resolvable. They
  are used only for the plot and the re-fit check, never to set a parameter.
* **The Simcyp PBPK layer is not packaged** (see Scope).
